subject: NetWell connection-mode heatmap, recommendation, and action items
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Samir Shah <samir.shah@netwell.io>, Alicia Rao <alicia@netwell-ops.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: NetWell: connectivity selection kickoff (peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S)

Hi all,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. NetWell has shared a short requirements spreadsheet (attached) and asked us for a pragmatic recommendation: whether to pursue VPC Peering, AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints), or a site-to-site (S2S) VPN/DirectConnect style tunnel for their Redwood Private deployment. Key constraints from the sheet: overlapping on-prem CIDRs, strict outbound egress controls (no direct internet from inference hosts), SOC2 evidence requirements, and preference for predictable SLA-backed throughput on inference traffic.

High level ask: can the three of us review the attached requirements and the rough heatmap I sketched, then confirm a recommended pattern plus a short PoC plan (1-2 week sandbox) for NetWell?

Attachments: netwell_connection_requirements.xlsx

What I think we should capture in the recommendation:
- Security posture (least privilege, isolation, IP exposure)
- Operational complexity / ownership (who troubleshoots routing/NAT)
- Production QoS (latency, throughput predictability)
- Compatibility with overlapping CIDRs and multi-account setup
- Required evidence/artifacts for NetWell's audit (route tables, flow logs, KMS usage)

I sketched a simple heatmap and dropped a work-in-progress PDF in Drive (link below). Please reply with your initial read and any red flags. If we align, I'll circle back to NetWell with the proposed next steps and timeline.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cNetWellPoc
HubSpot: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/NW-4821

Thanks,
Logan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Samir Shah <samir.shah@netwell.io>, Alicia Rao <alicia@netwell-ops.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NetWell: connectivity selection kickoff (peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S)

Logan — thanks for pulling this together. Quick read through the requirements + the CIDR overlap note. My high-level take: avoid classic VPC Peering for the primary dataplane because of IP overlap and two-way routing requirements across NetWell accounts; peering forces unique, non-overlapping address spaces or NAT to work around overlaps which adds brittle NAT transforms and makes traceability worse for audits.

I put a short comparative heatmap here (quick scores, 1-5 where 5 is best):
- VPC Peering: latency 4, security 3, overlap tolerance 1, operational surface 2, cross-account control 2
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints): latency 3, security 5, overlap tolerance 5, operational surface 4, cross-account control 5
- S2S VPN (BGP/static): latency 2-3 (variable), security 4 (with IPsec), overlap tolerance 3 (can NAT), operational surface 3, cross-account control 3

My recommendation: a split-control pattern — use PrivateLink for the Redwood control plane/service endpoints so NetWell's control traffic (model selection, metrics, console API) is strongly isolated and works with overlapping addresses. For the heavy inference dataplane we can provision an S2S IPSec tunnel (or DirectConnect if they want consistent bandwidth) that routes only the inference egress/ingress via a dedicated subnet with NAT and BGP; this avoids putting all traffic over the interface endpoints and gives predictable bandwidth options.

Pros of this hybrid:
- PrivateLink minimizes cross-account IP footprint and preserves least-privilege service exposure.
- S2S allows us to respect NetWell's on-prem routing/eBGP requirements and keeps large data flows on a managed tunnel.
- We can provide SOC2 artifacts separately: endpoint logs for PrivateLink, flow logs for the tunnel, and a documented NAT mapping table.

Cons / risks:
- Slightly higher ops cost (two connectivity patterns to support).
- Double-hop/egress NAT must be tested for source-IP preservation if NetWell requires it for downstream firewalling.

I'll attach a short pdf with the heatmap and a proposed PoC checklist. If Samir/Alicia confirm the DirectConnect/ExpressRoutes option isn't required upfront, we can start the PoC with IPsec tunnels and evaluate throughput.

Attachment: connectivity-heatmap-v1.pdf

-Kim
Principal Network Architect, Redwood Private
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@netwell.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Alicia Rao <alicia@netwell-ops.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NetWell: connectivity selection kickoff (peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S)

Thanks, Logan and Kim — clear write-up. A couple of clarifications from NetWell side:
1) We definitely cannot change on-prem CIDRs in the short term (legacy kit). That rules out peering unless we accept heavy NAT.
2) For throughput: our inference burst pattern can hit sustained 400-600 Mbps. DirectConnect would be ideal but we need cost justification; can IPsec tunnels handle predictable bursts for a PoC?
3) For compliance: we need explicit evidence that no inference data leaves the Redwood-PoP without transiting our egress controls (we have perimeter DLP). So any NAT or flow path needs to be auditable.

If the hybrid approach is the recommendation, please confirm a minimal PoC plan (what we'll configure, test cases, success criteria) and a rough timeline. We can commit an on-prem engineer and a small cloud environment for the trial next week.

-Samir
Network Architect, NetWell Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@netwell.io>, Alicia Rao <alicia@netwell-ops.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T15:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NetWell: connectivity selection kickoff (peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S)

Appreciate the fast responses — summary + next steps below.

Summary (agree with Kim): hybrid pattern = PrivateLink for control plane + IPsec S2S tunnel for inference dataplane (DirectConnect optional for production). Reason: overlapping CIDRs, auditability, and predictable heavy flows.

PoC plan (1 week sandbox):
- Day 0: Redwood creates a sandbox PrivateLink endpoint service and a lightweight control plane image. NetWell provides an on-prem VM + public IP for tunnel peer.
- Day 1-2: Establish IPsec tunnel (IKEv2) with policy-based or BGP (prefer BGP if NetWell can). Configure route filters so only inference subnet is routed to the tunnel.
- Day 3: Run throughput tests with 0.5-1.0 Gbps simulated load; capture metrics.
- Day 4: Validate audit buckets: VPC flow logs, PrivateLink access logs, and NAT mapping table exported to NetWell.
- Success criteria: stable 400 Mbps sustained for 5 minutes, end-to-end path documented, and evidence artifacts generated for SOC2 reviewer.

Action items:
- NetWell: confirm they can provide an on-prem peer public IP + BGP ASN and a windows/linux VM for testing (Samir).
- Logan: open a PoC ticket and provision a sandbox endpoint service + minimal docs (Logan).
- Kim: prepare a one-pager SOC2 checklist and the NAT mapping template (Kim).
- Ben: I'll own the mutual action plan doc and follow-up scheduling (link attached).

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.docx
Related links: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/NW-4821

I'll schedule a 30-min sync for Monday morning and include lab credentials. Thanks everyone — we'll iterate after the PoC run.

-Ben
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
